Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system

Class StorageService

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.StorageService
public final class StorageService extends Object
Read-only block-device discovery for the LFS/BLFS storage manager, normative in system-management-contract.md §4.5. It builds the lsblk argument vector and parses its -P key/value output; it never re-implements device discovery and never mutates anything (LUKS mutations live in LuksService).

The command-building and parsing are pure and unit-testable (buildListCommand(), parseDevices(List), buildUuidCommand(String)); listDevices() is a thin wrapper over ProcessRunner. State files (/etc/crypttab, /etc/fstab) are read-only for the GUI (§3.5); writes go through cryptsetup/the installer helper, never direct edits (§6).

  • Method Details

    • isAvailable

      public static boolean isAvailable()
      True if lsblk is present on this host.

    • buildListCommand

      public static List<String> buildListCommand()
      Builds the read-only list vector: lsblk -P -o <columns>. The -P key/value form is stable to parse and needs no --no-color (lsblk does not colourise a pipe).

    • buildUuidCommand

      public static List<String> buildUuidCommand(String device)
      Builds the read-only UUID probe vector for a device: blkid -s UUID -o value <device>. Returns an empty list for a blank device.

    • parseDevices

      public static List<StorageService.BlockDevice> parseDevices(List<String> lines)
      Parses lsblk -P output lines into StorageService.BlockDevice values. Each line is a set of KEY="value" pairs; blank lines are dropped and parsing never throws.

    • listDevices

      public static List<StorageService.BlockDevice> listDevices()
      Lists the block devices, read-only. Returns an empty list when lsblk is absent (a non-Linux/dev host) rather than throwing.

    • readUuid

      public static String readUuid(String device)
      Reads a device's UUID, read-only. Returns an empty string when blkid is absent or the device has no UUID.
